title: Air Assist Display & PSI Adjustment Fix
body_html:
Air Assist Digital Display Abnormality & Adjustment Failure - Hydra GEN2 Series

This guide explains how to troubleshoot abnormal air assist display behavior and airflow adjustment failures on ONELASER laser machines. It covers common causes such as air leaks, disconnected tubing, regulator issues, display configuration errors, and faulty electrical connections, along with step-by-step solutions to restore proper airflow control.

Problem Description

1. Rotating the air assist knob clockwise or counter-clockwise results in no significant change on the digital display (fluctuations remain minimal, around ±0.1 PSI).

2. After pressing the red test button, the display remains red regardless of adjustment settings.

 

Cause

  • Open Air Circuit: The external air source is off, an internal tube has detached, or there is a leak preventing pressure buildup.
  • Electrical Connection: Loose wiring or poor contact at the back of the digital display.
  • Configuration Error: Internal parameters of the digital display were accidentally modified.
  • Mechanical Lock: The regulator knob is in the "locked" position or the internal mechanical valve is damaged.

Solution

Method 1. Inspect the External Air Source

Step 1. Check the Pump/Compressor

Ensure the air pump is powered on and running. 

  • Check the air pump specifications. If the pump is too small, the adjustment effect may not be obvious.
  • Check the air pump’s own pressure gauge (if it has) to ensure the output pressure is within the machine's required range.

Step 2. Check External Tubing

Inspect the air tube from the air pump to the machine's Air Inlet for kinks or cuts.

Unplug and re-insert the air tube connector to ensure it is firmly seated in place.

Method 2. Inspect the Internal Air Circuit

Step 1. Check Tubing Inside the Machine

Open the side panel and inspect the air tubes between the back of the digital display, the solenoid valve, and the regulator valve. Check specifically for tubes that may have slipped off due to long-term vibration or airflow blockages caused by an excessively small bending radius.

Step 2. Check the Solenoid Valve Outlet

Disconnect the air tube at the solenoid valve outlet and feel if there is a strong airflow being ejected. If not, the solenoid valve is damaged or not receiving a trigger signal.

Step 3. Check the Regulator Valve Outlet

With the air source connected, turn the adjustment knob. Disconnect the air tube leading from the regulator valve to the cutting head and test whether the airflow intensity changes as the knob is turned. If the airflow remains constant or there is no air output, the pressure regulator valve is internally damaged.

Method 3. Check the Digital Display

Step 1. Check the Digital Display Settings (Factory Standard)

Note: If you need to change options or values in the settings during this process, you must first set 1-P and 2-P in Step ② to 0.

① Long-press the SET key to enter the settings menu. Click the SET key to switch between setting items, and use the Up/Down keys next to it to change options/values. Verify the settings match the table below:

② Click the SET key again and set the values for 1-P and 2-P to 0.3. This value determines at what pressure the display changes color, typically used to indicate if the airflow meets working requirements.

 

Step 2. Check the Mechanical Status of Buttons and Knobs

If you find the display lights up even without pressing the red button, please troubleshoot according to this FAQ: Test button always on, unable to adjust airflow

The adjustment knobs on the Hydra Gen2 usually feature a "pull up to unlock, press down to lock" design. If you cannot rotate it, try gently pulling the knob upward. If it is stuck, you can use a tool to help pull it up, after which it should return to normal operation.

Step 3. Check the Wiring at the Back

Inspect the plug or wiring terminals behind the digital display. Gently tug the cables to confirm the terminal screws are tightened. If the wiring has poor contact, the digital display may show jumping values or a black screen due to unstable voltage.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please click this link to submit a support ticket: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
